Edge case: IMovieCatalogRepository check-then-insert pattern has a TOCTOU race in concurrent scenarios — implementation must address this.

comments.note: IMovieCatalogRepository has a TOCTOU (check-then-act) race between MovieExistsAsync and InsertMovieAsync. Two concurrent callers could both see false from MovieExistsAsync and then both attempt InsertMovieAsync, causing a duplicate-key error. The interface contract only says 'callers should check first'; the implementation should handle this via transaction isolation or INSERT IGNORE semantics.

IRefreshOrchestrator.StartRefreshAsync returns an immediately-completed Task when a refresh is already running. Callers cannot await the end of the in-progress refresh via this call alone — they must poll State or subscribe to events. This is an intentional design decision per the Developer's notes, but the Reviewer should confirm the UI/consumer needs are met.
No observations beyond the above — all 12 files follow clean BCL-only sealed record / interface patterns consistent with the existing Core codebase.

summary: Code review PASS with two Fix-Forward edits applied. All 12 Core contract files are well-structured, BCL-only, and follow established conventions. Enums are exhaustive and well-documented. Model records use required/init-only properties correctly (LibraryFolder, RefreshSummary) and document nullable semantics clearly. All 7 interfaces use cancellation tokens consistently, nullable parameters default to null, and BCL collection types (IReadOnlyList, IReadOnlyDictionary, IReadOnlyCollection) are used throughout. Fix 1: InsertMovieAsync doc replaced misleading check-then-act guidance with an implementation-side concurrency contract. Fix 2: StartRefreshAsync return doc clarified to explicitly describe the already-completed-task no-op behavior. Build confirmed clean at 0 warnings after edits.

comments.note: IMovieCatalogRepository.InsertMovieAsync: replaced 'Callers should check MovieExistsAsync first to avoid duplicate-key errors' with a <remarks> block that places the concurrency contract on the implementation side — 'Implementations must handle duplicate-key scenarios gracefully (e.g., via INSERT IGNORE or ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE semantics) because concurrent callers cannot safely rely on a prior MovieExistsAsync check to prevent races.' The original guidance encouraged a check-then-act pattern that cannot be made safe without DB-level atomicity.

IRefreshOrchestrator.StartRefreshAsync <returns> doc: reworded from 'A Task that completes when the refresh finishes (or when it was already running and this call was a no-op)' to explicitly state that the no-op case returns an already-completed task and directs callers to monitor State or LastSummary to track a running instance. Non-behavioral change; build confirmed clean at 0 warnings.

RefreshProgress.Total uses int (0 = not-yet-known) vs int? semantics. The doc-comment documents this convention correctly. A nullable int? would be more explicit but changing the type is out of scope for a Fix-Forward — flag for a future API review if ambiguity causes consumer bugs.

IVideoHasher.ComputeHashAsync passes IObfuscationMap as a call-site parameter rather than constructor injection. The Developer's rationale (test isolation without DI rewiring) is valid. If the obfuscation map ever becomes expensive to construct, caching at the scanner level will be the natural fix.

[documentation-forward] IMovieCatalogRepository: the AddFilenameAsync method lacks a <remarks> note similar to the one now on InsertMovieAsync. While the TOCTOU risk is lower (the filename uniqueness constraint is softer), adding a brief concurrency guidance note would make the contract symmetric. Documentation agent should add it.

notes: All 12 Core contract files created. No PackageReferences added to VideoIndexer.Core. 0 warnings, 0 errors. All 161 tests pass.

Key design decisions: IMovieCatalogRepository exposes fine-grained exists/insert primitives rather than a single upsert, to keep the business logic in LibraryScanner. IRefreshOrchestrator returns Task from StartRefreshAsync that resolves when the run finishes; LastSummary holds the roll-up.
IVideoHasher.ComputeHashAsync takes IObfuscationMap as a parameter (not injected via constructor) so tests can substitute maps without rewiring DI.

WP-002 passes QA. All 5 ACs met: 12 files present and correctly placed, Core.csproj has zero PackageReferences, build clean, 161 tests pass.
